what: Tesla is the largest US electric-car maker (Model 3, Y, S, X and Cybertruck) and also builds large battery storage systems. It invests heavily in self-driving, robotaxis and the Optimus humanoid robot.
customers: Car buyers in the US, Europe and China, and utilities and energy projects for its Megapack batteries.
money: direct car sales without dealers, plus regulatory credits sold to other carmakers
Megapack and Powerwall batteries; growing with good margins
Superchargers, repairs, insurance and Full Self-Driving software
moat: A strong brand, a large charging network, low production costs and driving data from millions of cars to train its self-driving AI.
risks: Falling EV prices and fierce competition, especially from China
A valuation that depends on robotaxis and Optimus succeeding
Dependence on Elon Musk and self-driving regulation
opportunities: Cash of about $45 billion far exceeds its debt
Energy storage deployments have been growing much faster than vehicles
Its driver assistance software, if approved for unsupervised use, would change the economics entirely
watch: Vehicle deliveries, automotive gross margin, and energy storage deployments.
